Boom CAN Bus ΓÇö Electrical Theory of Operation (Section 240, Group 20D)
GWC ΓÇö Electrical Diagnostic (Section 245, Group 50)
GWC ΓÇö Electrical Theory of Operation (Section 245, Group 20)
Refer to the electrical schematic.
7.
Visually verify that relevant fuses are not blown.
1.
Identify relevant power and ground/return circuits.
2.
Test for proper voltage on the potentially faulty component, between the power circuit and the ground
/return circuit.
8.
If the test between the power circuit and the ground/return circuit is bad, test for voltage
between the power circuit and a frame ground.
1.
If the test between the power circuit and the ground/return circuit is bad, but the test between
the power circuit and the frame ground is good, then the issue is on the ground/return circuit.
2.
If the test between the power circuit and the ground/return circuit is bad, and the test between
the power circuit and the frame ground is bad, then the issue is on the power circuit.
3.
Refer to the electrical schematic. Narrow down any circuit issues to the root cause. Refer to Circuit
 (Section 240, Group 10).
Checks
9.
Reprogram the control unit. Refer toControl Unit Reprogramming(Section 245, Group 10C).
10.
Refer to the electrical system diagnostic.
11.

GWC 001235.11 ΓÇö Addressing Fault with Gateway Control 
Unit
One or more See & Spray vision processing control unit (VPU) has an addressing failure with the gateway 
control unit (GWC) on controller area network (CAN) binary unit system (bus) 3.
The See & Spray VPUs cannot claim an address with GWC on the BoomTrac CAN bus. One or more faulted
See & Spray VPUs are disabled. Cycling power may re-establish communication.
Addressing requires proper functioning power, ground, addressing, and CAN circuits. Diagnose and repair
CAN circuits, starting with first faulted control units. Identify the fault location within the Diagnostic Center
application under See & SprayΓÇöImage Processor/Camera.
Component Information:

See & Spray Addressing ΓÇö Electrical Schematic(Section 240, Group 30L)

 (Section 211, Group 05).

ΓÇó

VPU closest to the center.
Fault occurs at startup if a VPU did not claim an address on the BoomTrac CAN.

addressing fault.

2.

a solid green indicator light if the VPU is powered and connected to BoomTrac CAN.
1.
From the center of the machine, diagnose the issue between last VPU without an addressing fault and
the first VPU with an addressing fault. For example, if VPU 8 is online and VPUs 9 and 10 have
addressing faults, check the sync circuits between VPUs 8 and 9.

Internal communication fault during startup. The See & Spray control unit reverted to fallback mode.

configured for See & Spray, including selecting a compatible nozzle part number. The system requires
input from the StarFire receiver, boom height sensors, and inertial measurement unit (IMU) sensors. Verify
that the components are calibrated and perform troubleshooting on any active codes. Cycle power to
attempt recovery.

1548
[TOC-ANCHOR:sec-09001faa85c435d1]
GWC 001672.02 ΓÇö Sync Line Communication Failure
A See & Spray control unit has a sync line failure.
The See & Spray control unit has not received the addressing frequency signal from the adjacent See &
Spray control unit to the left. Addressing requires functioning sync circuits. The See & Spray system is
disabled.
Component Information:
Vision Processing Unit (VPU) Assemblies
W0087 ΓÇö Center Frame Sensing Harness
W0105 ΓÇö Left-Hand Inner Wing Sensing Harness
W0106 ΓÇö Right-Hand Inner Wing Sensing Harness
Schematic:
See & Spray CAN Bus ΓÇö Electrical Schematic(Section 240, Group 30L)
Diagnostic Steps:
There is a sync line fault. The likely cause is a power disruption to the most inboard vision processing unit
(VPU) that is not addressed or a harness failure between the last addressed VPU and the first non-
addressed VPU.
Related information:
See & Spray Addressing ΓÇö Electrical Schematic(Section 240, Group 30L)
Verify that the code is still active. Refer to 
 (Section 211, Group 05). If
Recall, Record, and Clear Codes
inactive, refer to 
 (Section 211, Group 05).
Intermittent Diagnostic Trouble Code Diagnostics
1.
Ensure that all control units are communicating on the applicable network or subnet.
2.
Refer to the display's Diagnostic Center application > applicable CAN network (when available).
1.
Refer to the display's Diagnostic Center application > Controllers > and verify that message
counts are changing on all control units along the applicable network or subnet.
2.
Identify which VPUs are online.
3.
If the VPUs are not shown as online, refer to the appropriate See & Spray schematic and diagnose the
power, ground, and controller area network (CAN) circuits for the VPUs that are not online, starting
with the VPUs closest to the ones that are online.
4.
Diagnose and repair the sync circuit at the first VPU reporting as faulted, going from left to right as
facing the rear of the machine.
5.
Check for a failed harness or faulty components between the last addressed VPU and the first non-
addressed VPU. Refer to the component locations. Visually check all connectors, components, and
harnesses for corrosion, binding, and damage. Repair or replace as necessary.
6.

GWC 001672.11 ΓÇö Addressing Fault with GWC
A See & Spray control unit or units has an addressing failure with the gateway control unit (GWC).
The See & Spray control unit cannot claim an address with the GWC on controller area network (CAN)
binary unit system (bus) 7. More than one control unit is requesting the same address. See & Spray system
is disabled.
Schematic:
Boom CAN Bus ΓÇö Electrical Schematic(Section 240, Group 30D)
Implement CAN Bus ΓÇö Electrical Schematic(Section 240, Group 30D)
See & Spray AddressingΓÇö Electrical Schematic(Section 240, Group 30L)
Diagnostic Steps:
Related information:
Boom CAN Bus ΓÇö Electrical Diagnostic (Section 240, Group 50D)
Implement CAN Bus ΓÇö Electrical Diagnostic (Section 240, Group 50D)
Verify that the code is still active. Refer to 
 (Section 211, Group 05). If
Recall, Record, and Clear Codes
inactive, refer to 
 (Section 211, Group 05).
Intermittent Diagnostic Trouble Code Diagnostics
1.
Cycle the key switch to reboot the system, clear out error messages, and re-establish proper
communication messages.
2.
Ensure that the GWC is communicating with all necessary control units on the implement CAN bus.
3.
Refer to the display's Diagnostic Center application > applicable CAN network (when available).
1.
Refer to the display's Diagnostic Center application > Controllers > and verify that message
counts are changing on all control units along the applicable network or subnet.
2.
If the GWC is not showing diagnostic addresses or very few are listed, diagnose any possible
implement CAN bus issues or BoomTrac CAN bus issues.
3.
Make note of which VPUs are online and which VPUs are offline. Verify if missing VPU was recently
added or reprogrammed.
4.
If the offline VPU is newly added, verify the payload version and that the payload was completely
loaded. Refer toVPU Reprogramming(Section 245, Group 10C) and attempt to reprogram VPU.
1.
If the offline VPU was recently reprogrammed, refer toVPU Reprogramming(Section 245, Group
10C) and attempt to reprogram the VPU.
2.
Refer to the electrical schematic. Narrow down CAN bus issues to the root cause. Refer to See & Spray
 (Section 240, Group 50L).
Addressing ΓÇö Electrical Diagnostic
5.
Always visually check all connectors, components, and harnesses for corrosion, binding, and damage.
6.

 (Section 240, Group 50L).
Addressing ΓÇö Electrical Diagnostic
5.

GWC 001672.12 ΓÇö CAN Communication Fault
The See & Spray controller area network (CAN) binary unit system (bus) has a communication fault.
The gateway controller (GWC) is unable to communicate with the faulted See & Spray control unit.
Communication requires functioning power, ground, and CAN bus circuits. The associated nozzles reverted
to the selected fallback mode.
Component Information:
XR601 ΓÇö BoomTrac Controller Area Network (CAN) Bus Terminator
XR602 ΓÇö BoomTrac Controller Area Network (CAN) Bus Terminator
Nozzle Assemblies (NZC)
Vision Processing Unit (VPU) Assemblies
W0080 ΓÇö Center Frame Dual Product Harness
W0087 ΓÇö Center Frame Sensing Harness
W0093 ΓÇö Left-Hand Inner Wing 1 Harness
W0094 ΓÇö Right-Hand Inner Wing 1 Harness
W0095 ΓÇö Left-Hand Inner Wing 2 Harness
W0096 ΓÇö Right-Hand Inner Wing 2 Harness
W0098 ΓÇö Right-Hand Outer Wing Harness
W0101 ΓÇö Left-Hand Breakaway Harness
W0102 ΓÇö Right-Hand Breakaway Harness
W0105 ΓÇö Left-Hand Inner Wing Sensing Harness
W0106 ΓÇö Right-Hand Inner Wing Sensing Harness
Schematic:
Boom CAN Bus ΓÇö Electrical Schematic(Section 240, Group 30D)
Diagnostic Steps:
Verify that the code is still active. Refer to 
 (Section 211, Group 05). If
Recall, Record, and Clear Codes
inactive, refer to 
 (Section 211, Group 05).
Intermittent Diagnostic Trouble Code Diagnostics
1.
Disconnect any third-party devices from the applicable CAN bus, local interconnect network (LIN) bus,
or CAN subnet.
2.
Disconnect the machine battery and reconnect the machine battery. This process reboots the system,
clears out error messages, and re-establishes proper communication messages.
3.
Utilize Service ADVISOR to ensure that all control units have the proper software. Update software as
necessary. Refer toControl Unit Reprogramming(Section 245, Group 10C).
4.

GWC002157.09 ΓÇö Source Address 162 Message Missing
See & Spray control unit 1 (VPU1) was not detected. The gateway control unit (GWC) is no longer receiving 
messages from the See & Spray control unit. The associated nozzles reverted to the selected fallback mode.
NOTE:
At powerup, allow 2ΓÇö3 minutes for active diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs) to appear on the
display.
This DTC may change to 1235.11 after a key cycle. Diagnose any 21xx.09 DTCs first, then
address any 1235.11 DTCs.
The vision processing unit (VPU) must be communicating properly and then lose communication with the
GWC for this DTC to be active. This can be caused by loss of switched or unswitched power at pins L3/M3,
grounds at pins L4/M4, or BoomTrac controller area network (CAN) high/low at pins F3/F4 to the affected
VPU.
Viewing the camera feed after completing the addressing procedure at start-up is a quick way to isolate
whether the cause of the DTC is a power and ground issue or a CAN issue. If the camera feed is showing
properly for a faulted VPU, then power and ground to the camera with the key ON and the engine ON is
present.
The following are necessary for this diagnostic procedure:

Does the fault message display as active?

GWC 002159.09 ΓÇö Source Address 162 Message Missing
See & Spray control unit 3 (VPU3) was not detected. The gateway control unit (GWC) is no longer receiving 
messages from the See & Spray control unit. The associated nozzles reverted to the selected fallback mode.
NOTE:
At powerup, allow 2ΓÇö3 minutes for active diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs) to appear on the
display.
This DTC may change to 1235.11 after a key cycle. Diagnose any 21xx.09 DTCs first, then
address any 1235.11 DTCs.
The vision processing unit (VPU) must be communicating properly and then lose communication with the
GWC for this DTC to be active. This can be caused by loss of switched or unswitched power at pins L3/M3,
grounds at pins L4/M4, or BoomTrac controller area network (CAN) high/low at pins F3/F4 to the affected
VPU.
Viewing the camera feed after completing the addressing procedure at start-up is a quick way to isolate
whether the cause of the DTC is a power and ground issue or a CAN issue. If the camera feed is showing
properly for a faulted VPU, then power and ground to the camera with the key ON and the engine ON is
present.
The following are necessary for this diagnostic procedure:
Schematic:

/M3 are approximately 11.4ΓÇö14 V on connector XA713-1 of the affected VPU. Repair the circuits.

BoomTrac CAN high/low are 2.5ΓÇö3.5 V and 1.5ΓÇö2.5 V on connector XA713-1 of the affected VPU. Repair the 
circuits.

GWC 002162.09 ΓÇö Source Address 162 Message Missing
See & Spray control unit (VPU 6) was not detected. The gateway control unit (GWC) is no longer receiving 
messages from the See & Spray control unit. The associated nozzles reverted to the selected fallback mode.
NOTE:
At powerup, allow 2ΓÇö3 minutes for active diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs) to appear on the
display.
This DTC may change to 1235.11 after a key cycle. Diagnose any 21xx.09 DTCs first, then
address any 1235.11 DTCs.
The vision processing unit (VPU) must be communicating properly and then lose communication with the
GWC for this DTC to be active. This can be caused by loss of switched or unswitched power at pins L3/M3,
grounds at pins L4/M4, or BoomTrac controller area network (CAN) high/low at pins F3/F4 to the affected
VPU.
Viewing the camera feed after completing the addressing procedure at start-up is a quick way to isolate
whether the cause of the DTC is a power and ground issue or a CAN issue. If the camera feed is showing
properly for a faulted VPU, then power and ground to the camera with the key ON and the engine ON is
present.
The following are necessary for this diagnostic procedure:
Schematic:
Boom CAN Bus ΓÇö Electrical Schematic (Section 240, Group 30D)
See & Spray Power and Ground ΓÇö Electrical Schematic(Section 240, Group 30L)
┬á

Action:

Does the fault message display as active?
Result:
YES:

Action:
NOTE:
VPUs 1ΓÇö9 are shown as a number, such as VPU1. VPUs 10 and above are shown as a letter,
such as VPUA. The lead VPU is shown as VPU 6.
Navigate to the diagnostic address(es) of the faulted VPU.
Does the affected VPU show on the CAN bus and have messages counting up?
Result:
YES:
This points toward a power/ground issue between the GWC and affected VPU. Refer to the See & Spray 
Power and Ground ΓÇö Electrical Schematic (Section 240, Group 30L). Verify that the power supply on pins L3
/M3 are approximately 11.4ΓÇö14 V on connector XA716-1 of the affected VPU. Repair the circuits.
NO:
This points toward a CAN high/low issue between the GWC and affected VPU. Verify that pins F3/F4 for 
BoomTrac CAN high/low are 2.5ΓÇö3.5 V and 1.5ΓÇö2.5 V on connector XA716-1 of the affected VPU. Repair the 
circuits.

GWC for this DTC to be active. This can be caused by loss of switched or unswitched power at pins L3/M3,
grounds at pins L4/M4, or BoomTrac controller area network (CAN) high/low at pins F3/F4 to the affected
VPU.
Viewing the camera feed after completing the addressing procedure at start-up is a quick way to isolate
whether the cause of the DTC is a power and ground issue or a CAN issue. If the camera feed is showing
properly for a faulted VPU, then power and ground to the camera with the key ON and the engine ON is
present.

Action:

YES:
This points toward a power/ground issue between the GWC and affected VPU. Refer to the See & Spray 
Power and Ground ΓÇö Electrical Schematic (Section 240, Group 30L). Verify that the power supply on pins L3
/M3 are approximately 11.4ΓÇö14 V on connector XA719-1 of the affected VPU. Repair the circuits.
NO:
This points toward a CAN high/low issue between the GWC and affected VPU. Verify that pins F3/F4 for 
BoomTrac CAN high/low are 2.5ΓÇö3.5 V and 1.5ΓÇö2.5 V on connector XA719-1 of the affected VPU. Repair the 
circuits.

 (Section
Intermittent Diagnostic Trouble Code Diagnostics
211, Group 05).

2.

3.

 (Section 245, Group 10C).
Reprogramming
1.

assistance center (DTAC). Refer to 
(Section 210, Group 100).

GWC 518216.02 ΓÇö Sync Line Communication Failure
The See & Spray control unit has not received the addressing frequency signal from the adjacent See & 
Spray control unit to the left.
The control unit has reverted to the last known address position to allow the See & Spray system to
function. Control units downstream may report as faulted. For replaced control units, an address line is
required for initial startup for See & Spray to function.
Component Information:
Vision Processing Unit (VPU) Assemblies
W0087 ΓÇö Center Frame Sensing Harness
W0105 ΓÇö Left-Hand Inner Wing Sensing Harness
W0106 ΓÇö Right-Hand Inner Wing Sensing Harness
Schematic:
See & Spray AddressingΓÇö Electrical Schematic(Section 240, Group 30L)
Diagnostic Steps:
There is a sync line fault. The likely cause is a power disruption to the most inboard vision processing unit
(VPU) that is not addressed or a harness failure between the last addressed VPU and the first non-
addressed VPU.
Related information:
Verify that the code is still active. Refer to 
 (Section 211, Group 05). If
Recall, Record, and Clear Codes
inactive, refer to 
 (Section 211, Group 05).
Intermittent Diagnostic Trouble Code Diagnostics
1.
Ensure that all control units are communicating on the applicable network or subnet.
2.
Refer to the display's Diagnostic Center application > applicable CAN network (when available).
1.
Refer to the display's Diagnostic Center application > Controllers > and verify that message
counts are changing on all control units along the applicable network or subnet.
2.
Identify which VPUs are online.
3.
If the VPUs are not shown as online, refer to the appropriate See & Spray schematic and diagnose the
power, ground, and controller area network (CAN) circuits for the VPUs that are not online, starting
with the VPUs closest to the ones that are online.
4.
Diagnose and repair the sync circuit at the first VPU reporting as faulted, going from left to right as
facing the rear of the machine.
5.
Check for a failed harness or faulty components between the last addressed VPU and the first non-
addressed VPU. Refer to the component locations. Visually check all connectors, components, and
harnesses for corrosion, binding, and damage. Repair or replace as necessary.
6.

GWC 518276.14 ΓÇö Control Unit Software is Out of Date
There is a See & Spray software mismatch.
The See & Spray control unit has determined the software is incompatible with the other control units
necessary for the system to function. The associated nozzles reverted back to the selected fallback mode.
Component Information:
Vision Processing Unit (VPU) Assemblies
Schematic:
VPU ΓÇö Electrical Schematic(Section 245, Group 30)
Diagnostic Steps:
Related information:
See & Spray Ethernet and FAKRA ΓÇö Electrical Theory of Operation (Section 240, Group 20L)
See & Spray Ethernet and FAKRA ΓÇö Electrical Diagnostic (Section 240, Group 50L)
VPU ΓÇö Electrical Diagnostic (Section 245, Group 50)
VPU ΓÇö Electrical Theory of Operation (Section 245, Group 20)
Identify the faulted VPU. On the display, select the Menu icon, System tab, Diagnostic Center icon,
System Diagnostics tab, and then See & SprayΓÇöImage Processor/Camera.
1.
Reprogram the faulted VPU. Refer toVPU Reprogramming(Section 245, Group 10C).
2.
Verify that the code is still active. Refer to 
 (Section 211, Group 05). If
Recall, Record, and Clear Codes
inactive, refer to 
 (Section 211, Group 05).
Intermittent Diagnostic Trouble Code Diagnostics
3.
If the code is still active, utilize Service ADVISOR to ensure that all control units have the proper
software.
NOTE:
Check the software for the remaining VPUs, nozzle body control unit (NZC), gateway
control unit (GWC), and master nozzle control unit (MNC) first. If all of these control units
have the proper software or updating the software for these control units does not solve
the issue, verify that the remaining control units have the proper software and update as
needed.
4.
Reprogram the control units as needed. Refer toControl Unit Reprogramming(Section 245, Group 10C).
5.

GWC 518387.02 ΓÇö VPU CAN Communication Fault on 
ExactApply Subnet
See & Spray control unit(s) controller area network (CAN) communication fault on an ExactApply nozzle 
subnet.

Agitation ΓÇö Electrical Theory of Operation
NOTE:
System 1 uses the secondary solution system control (SSSC).
System 2 uses the primary solution system control (PSSC).
Agitation is used to keep chemicals mixed in the solution tank. Automatic and manual agitation can be
selected from the display. Agitation can be modified as necessary from the display when:
Component Information:
Agitation is activated by one of two ways:
When agitation is activated, the agitation level can be viewed on the corner post display (PDU).
Solution contents require more or less agitation.
ΓÇó
Manual control of agitation is desired. Operator turns off automatic agitation.
ΓÇó
Reduced risk of foaming at low solution levels is desired. Operator turns on automatic agitation.

[TOC-ANCHOR:sec-09001faa85b6adf4]
Eductor System 1 ΓÇö Electrical Theory of Operation
NOTE:
System 1 utilizes the secondary solution system control unit (SSSC).
The chemical eductor attachment allows the operator the ability to add pesticides, herbicides, and plant
nutrients to the tank from the ground. The eductor is a stainless-steel bowl with a 20 L (5.28 gal) capacity.
The eductor folds down from the storage position with spring assist to a comfortable working height.
When the eductor valve is open, the contents in the eductor are immediately drawn into the pressure line
through a venturi. Once in the venturi, the contents are carried to the solution tank. The design of the
bowl and location of the venturi ensure that all chemicals and other products are evacuated into the
solution tank.
Component Information:
The machine must first be in park before eduction can begin from the load center location on the side of
the machine. The operator station domain control unit (OSDC) monitors the position of the multi-function
lever. The position is broadcast over the implement controller area network (CAN) binary unit system (bus).
The OSDC reads the message and forwards the message to the SSSC.
When the eductor button is pressed on the dual system keypad, a message is broadcast on the implement
CAN bus to the SSSC. When the eductor button is pressed on the armrest, a message is broadcast on the
operator station domain (OSD) CAN bus to the OSDC. The OSDC receives the message and forwards it on
the implement CAN bus to the SSSC.
NOTE:
Tank sump valve and rinse nozzle eductor valve must be opened manually on machine
equipped with manual solution controls.
A101 ΓÇö Operator station domain control unit (OSDC)
ΓÇó
A102 ΓÇö CommandARM control unit (ARMC)
ΓÇó
A120 ΓÇö Corner post display (PDU)
ΓÇó
A121 ΓÇö Premium server
ΓÇó
A122 ΓÇö CommandCenter display
ΓÇó
A307 ΓÇö Secondary solution system control unit (SSSC)
ΓÇó
A311 ΓÇö Dual system keypad
ΓÇó

ΓÇó

operator station domain (OSD) CAN bus to the OSDC. The OSDC receives the message and forwards it on
the implement CAN bus to the PSSC.
NOTE:
Tank sump valve and rinse nozzle eductor valve must be opened manually on machine
equipped with manual solution controls.

PAGE 4198 | phrase: Boom CAN Bus

4198
To raise the right boom wing (tilt up), the right boom raise switch is selected on the multi-function lever.
When the right boom raise switch is held in a depressed state, a CAN bus message is supplied to the BCHU
from the multi-function lever. If the boom fold pedal is NOT depressed, the BCHU sends a pulse-width-
modulated (PWM) signal to the right tilt up solenoid valve. The right tilt up solenoid valve directs
pressurized oil to the rod end of the right tilt cylinder.
To lower the right boom wing (tilt down), the right boom lower switch is selected on the multi-function
lever. When the right boom lower switch is held in a depressed state, a CAN bus message is supplied to the
BCHU from the multi-function lever. If the boom fold pedal is NOT depressed, the BCHU sends a pulse-
width-modulated (PWM) signal to the right tilt down solenoid. The energized right tilt down solenoid valve
releases oil from the right tilt cylinder back to tank, thus allow gravity tilt down.
Tilt Accumulators and Tilt Accumulator Sensor
Each tilt cylinder will have a 2.0 L accumulator. The accumulators are filled with dry nitrogen that
compresses when pressure is applied, aiding the booms during folding and unfolding. Due to the sheer
length and mass of the booms, folding an d unfolding can cause stress on the center frame structure. The
tilt accumulator pressure sensor monitors each accumulator and sends messages to the BCHU. The BCHU
monitors the pressure from the tilt accumulator pressure sensor. When the pressure drops low enough,
the BCHU requests the powertrain domain control unit (PODC) to activate the load sense jam valve. The
accumulators can absorb some of the impact due to machine vibration, acting as a cushion for the
structure.
These accumulators are able to reduce the dynamic pressure spikes that occur when operating in various
field conditions protecting the structure and hydraulic components from harsh spikes during field
operations.
Refer to the appropriate Repair Technical Manual (RTM) for additional information on charge accumulators.
Related Information
Advanced Tilt Control ΓÇö Electrical Schematic(240-30B)
Boom CAN Bus ΓÇö Electrical Theory of Operation (240-20D)
Implement CAN Bus ΓÇö Electrical Theory of Operation (240-20D)
OSD CAN Bus ΓÇö Electrical Theory of Operation (240-20D)

PAGE 4207 | phrase: Boom CAN Bus
======================================================================
4207
The boom has seven ultrasonic height sensors (UHS). The sensors use ultrasonic signals to measure the
distance between the boom and the target. Each sensor is an electronic control unit, which sends the
boom height information as a controller area network (CAN) binary unit system (bus) message to the boom
control hydraulic unit (BCHU). The calibration procedure matches the sensor serial numbers with the
sensor position on the boom.
There are five inertial measurement units (IMUs) located on the boom (two on the left-hand boom, two on
the right-hand boom, and one on the center frame). These IMUs are on the same CAN bus as the (UHS)
boom sensors. The IMUs sense chassis movement and relays that information to the BCHU. The BCHU
reads the information and tries to counter those movements to stabilize the boom.
BoomTrac Ultimate uses a CAN bus system separate from the other networks on the sprayer. The boom
CAN bus for the BoomTrac Ultimate system communicates between the BCHU, IMU, and the height
sensors. The boom roll sensor measures the angle of the boom center frame.
The boom roll sensor is a hall effect sensor. The BCHU provides a voltage power to the sensor. The sensor
provides return information to the BCHU.
The multi-function lever receives input from the resume switch. The switch inputs are communicated from
the multi-function lever over the implement CAN bus. The BoomTrac system is deactivated by using the
boom fold, raise, or lower functions. The activation switch must be pressed again for BoomTrac to resume
functioning.
If the inner wings are folded, BoomTrac does not activate. Once the resume switch is pressed, pressing it
again adjusts the center frame to the target height if the BoomTrac setup is in the Control To Height mode.
The hydraulic system uses proportional valves for the boom tilt function to vary the flow rate to the
cylinders.
If issues are found with the BoomTrac system, perform calibration procedures. A valid and accurate
calibration is very important for proper operation. See the appropriate OperatorΓÇÖs Manual (OM) for
calibration procedures.
Related Information
BoomTrac Leveling ΓÇö Electrical Schematic(240-30B)
Boom CAN Bus ΓÇö Electrical Theory of Operation (240-20D)
Boom Tilt ΓÇö Hydraulic Theory of Operation (270-20D)

Corner Post Display ΓÇö Electrical Theory of Operation
The corner post display (PDU) on the right corner post shows the operator current machine functionality.
These functions include things like the lighting, turn signals, vehicle speed, fuel level, and engine coolant
temperature, which can be viewed while operating the machine.
Component Information:
Input for the PDU comes from commands sent from the CommandARM control unit (ARMC) and the
minipod assembly controls. When a function is selected, the operator station domain control unit (OSDC) is
notified. The OSDC broadcasts a controller area network (CAN) binary unit system (bus) message to the
display over the vehicle CAN bus.
There is an alarm buzzer equipped with the PDU. The alarm buzzer is an audible alarm that sounds when a
visual alarm appears on the display.
Battery power is provided through the PDU fuse. Ground for the PDU is provided by the battery box
ground 2.

[TOC-ANCHOR:sec-09001faa85a9eb6c]
Video ΓÇö Electrical Theory of Operation
The video system allows the operator to observe areas around the machine that are difficult to see from
the operator station. Video can be displayed when certain machine functions are performed, such as
reversing.
Component Information:
The 4600 processor can support up to four camera inputs. Even though there can be up to four camera
images available, only one image can be viewed at a time on the display. The video image can be displayed
on either the secondary display or on the main CommandCenter display.
Camera selection is available by both manual and automatic triggering. The touchscreen display provides
manual camera control. Automatic triggers can be set up with the specific machine functions, such as
reversing allowing view of the rear of the machine.
To activate the video, video icon is selected on the display or is selected on the navigation bar. A vehicle
controller area network (CAN) binary unit system (bus) message is sent from the premium server to the
CommandARM control unit (ARMC). The ARMC then sends activation allowing for the necessary battery
power to the camera. The switched power for the selected camera is provided from the operator station
domain control unit (OSDC). Camera ground is supplied from the battery box ground 2. Once the selected
camera receives power, the video image is fed back to the display.

PAGE 4247 | phrase: vision processing unit
======================================================================
4247
The boom control hydraulic unit (BCHU) functions as a gateway, connecting BoomTrac CAN bus with
implement CAN bus.
Each boom contains multiple cameras, ultrasonic height sensors (UHS), inertial measurement units (IMU),
and vision processing units (VPU). Information is processed by the VPU to command the spray action of the
nozzles. This includes images gathered by the cameras, boom pose information measured by the IMU,
boom distance away from the ground, and the crop canopy measured by the UHS. Each sensor is a
miniature electronic control unit that sends the gathered information as a binary (digital) CAN message to
the BCHU.
Accuracy increases as the boom gets lower. When the boom is at a greater height, singular weeds are
caught by more cameras. The VPU receives this information and commands multiple nozzles to spray,
which causes overlapping. When the boom is at a lower height, singular weeds are caught by fewer
cameras. The VPU receives this information and commands fewer nozzles to spray, which causes a more
precise application.
Related Information:

Implement CAN Bus ΓÇö Electrical Theory of Operation (240-20D)
VPU ΓÇö Electrical Theory of Operation (245-20)
BCHU ΓÇö Electrical Theory of Operation (245-20)

ExactApply CAN Bus ΓÇö Electrical Theory of Operation
Machines equipped with ExactApply (the solution spray nozzle system) are equipped with an ExactApply
controller area network binary unit system (CAN bus).
Component Information
CAN bus systems transfer messages between every control unit on the machine. These messages include
commands, requests, broadcast information, responses, acknowledgments, and various group functions.
The CAN bus is a linear network, and the control units are connected along its length in series.
The operator has no direct control of the CAN bus systems. CAN bus operates automatically whenever the
key switch is in the ACC, RUN, or START positions.
For information on the ExactApply CAN bus system, refer to the appropriate ExactApply Diagnostic
Technical Manual (DTM).

Implement CAN Bus ΓÇö Electrical Theory of Operation
The implement controller area network (CAN) binary unit system (bus) allows control units to send and
receive messages to and from one another using a two-wire system with two terminators. The two-wire
system provides the implement CAN bus high and implement CAN bus low signals.
Component Information:
The premium server, MTG, MNC, and SA port function as a gateway to connect the implement CAN bus and
vehicle CAN bus. The BCHU acts as a gateway to connect the implement CAN bus and BoomTrac CAN bus.
The OSDC acts as a gateway to connect implement CAN bus, vehicle CAN bus, operator station domain
(OSD) LIN bus, and operator station domain (OSD) CAN bus.

Aftertreatment ΓÇö Electrical Theory of Operation
The aftertreatment device (ATD) passively and actively captures the particulate matter (soot) from the
engine exhaust gas. The aftertreatment process cleans the engine of hydrocarbons and nitrogen oxide
(NOx). In total, the machine aftertreatment regenerates the engine exhaust, producing only clean nitrogen
gas and water vapor.
Component Information:
Exhaust gas enters the diesel oxidation catalyst (DOC) chamber and then flows through the diesel
particulate filter (DPF). The DOC actively oxidizes hydrocarbons, while the DPF passively captures
particulates. Constant monitoring of exhaust gas temperature allows the electronic control unit to manage
this regeneration process.
There are two aftertreatment NOx sensors. The NOx sensor, located at the DPF outlet, and the
aftertreatment outlet NOx sensor, located at the selective catalyst reduction (SCR) outlet. These sensors
monitor emission levels and machine NOx conversion efficiency. The engine control unit (ECU) provides
power for both sensors.
Information from these sensors, travels along the engine controller area network (CAN) binary unit system
(bus) high and low circuits and into the ECU. The ECU uses this information to assess the NOx conversion
efficiency.

PAGE 4257 | phrase: corner post display

4257
Diesel exhaust fluid (DEF) converts NOx into nitrogen gas and water vapor. The SCR injects a high purity
urea-based additive into the exhaust system cleaning the engine emissions.
The DEF fluid temperature sensor and DPF differential pressure sensor measures the initial output from
the turbocharger and DPF.
The DEF dosing injector then mixes high purity urea-based additive into the exhaust line, which converts
NOx into nitrogen and water.
DEF tank header assembly, SCR supply module, and DEF dosing line heaters (when in good working order),
allow the DEF dosing injector to function correctly. The DEF tank assembly allows coolant flow when
needed. It also measures the fluid level and temperature. DEF supply module pumps DEF from tank to the
dosing injector. When the temperature is cold, DEF dosing unit heater and DEF dosing line heaters keep
the lines from freezing.
The ECU powers and controls all DEF and SCR components. Signals return to the ECU and, when needed,
information passes to the corner post display (PDU) through CAN bus circuits.
For more detailed information on the aftertreatment system, see the appropriate engine component
technical manual (CTM).
Related Information:

Fuel Level Sender ΓÇö Electrical Theory of Operation
Fuel level is displayed on the corner post display as a segmented gauge for the operator. When the level
reaches 10% remaining fuel, the fuel indicator flashes, an alarm sounds, and a low fuel message appears.
Component Information:
The system is active whenever the key switch is in the RUN position.
The fuel level sender is a variable resistor that provides a signal output proportional to the fuel level in the
tank. The greater the fuek volume, the higher the resistance. When the fuel level is lowest, there is no
resistance across the sensor.
The powertrain domain control unit (PODC) monitors the fuel level and a vehicle controller area network
(CAN) binary unit system (bus) message is sent to the PDU where the fuel level is displayed.
For additional information, refer to the appropriate engine component technical manual (CTM).
Related Information:

Ethernet Configuration 2 ΓÇö Electrical Theory of Operation
Ethernet configuration 2 is an Ethernet switch used to communicate information between the Ethernet
configuration 1 Ethernet switch, the left- and right-hand cameras, and Ethernet switch 3 assembly.
Component Information:
Information gathered by the See & Spray cameras is transferred through the vision processing units
(VPUs). This information then goes through Ethernet switches 1 and 2 to Ethernet switch 3. Information
from Ethernet switch 3 is sent to the Ethernet configuration 2 Ethernet switch assembly along with
information from the left- and right-hand cameras.
Information gathered by the Ethernet configuration 2 Ethernet switch is then passed on to the Ethernet
configuration 1 Ethernet switch.
Ground for the Ethernet configuration 2 Ethernet switch is provided by the battery box ground.

JDLink Telematics ΓÇö Electrical Theory of Operation
The modular telematics gateway (MTG) is one of the main components that enable JDLink and
MyJohnDeere solutions. The MTG allows for data to transfer to and from the JDLink host server over a
cellular network or wireless network. An active JDLink subscription is required for JDLink and MyJohnDeere
services.
The MTG by default will remain powered for five minutes after the machine is powered off to allow any
queued tasks to complete on the MTG. Then the MTG enters a sleep state for up to seven days.
Component Information:
The MTG supports remote service capabilities. The technician uses John Deere Service ADVISOR remote to
service the machine control units remotely through the MTG. The MTG provides remote access to machine
information through software on an internet-based web browser from a personal computer.
Communication throughout the JDLink telematics system is provided by Ethernet, vehicle controller area
network (CAN) binary system unit (bus), and implement CAN bus.
The machine electrical system provides switch power through the MTG fuse. Ground is provided to the
JDLink telematics system by the battery box ground.
Related Information
JDLink Telematics ΓÇö Electrical Schematic (Section 240, Group 30F)

Premium Server and CommandCenter Display ΓÇö Electrical 
Theory of Operation
The premium server transfers information to and from monitors and video connectors.
Related Information:
The display server fuse provides power from the battery to the premium server. With supplied power from
the battery, the premium server turns on with wakeup power. The premium server provides
communication between the premium server and the vehicle controller area network (CAN) binary unit
system (bus) and implement CAN bus networks.
The premium server gathers information coming through video 1, 2, 3, and 4 connectors, and displays
relevent information on the CommandCenter display and auxiliary corner post display.
Using Ethernet, communication between the monitors and video connectors can return to the machine.
Ground for the premium server is provided by the battery box ground.

[TOC-ANCHOR:sec-09001faa860ececb]
Load Center: ExactApply ΓÇö Electrical Theory of Operation
The ExactApply (EA) load center provides electrical power to the See & Spray load center and also supplies
electrical power for all the EA electrical components, devices, and wiring.
Component Information
The EA load center is located at the rear of the machine. Power is supplied to the load center from the
master nozzle control unit/See & Spray fuse located in the rear mid-chassis cab load center.
Ground is supplied by the dual product center frame ground.

[TOC-ANCHOR:sec-09001faa86129ff2]
Hydraulic Oil Temperature and Level ΓÇö Electrical Theory of 
Operation
Maintaining a normal oil temperature in all hydraulic systems is important for successful system
operation. Maintaining a good hydraulic oil level also influences the oil temperature and performance of
the hydraulic components.
Component Information:
The powertrain domain control unit (PODC) monitors the hydraulic oil temperature. The hydraulic oil
temperature is shown on the corner post display (PDU) via the hydraulic oil temperature indicator. The
indicator will show in the green for normal operating conditions. As temperature increases the indicator
will advance to the red area. When the oil temperature starts to increase into a more critical range a yellow
caution indicator will display along with any diagnostic trouble codes. When oil temperature rises to the
extreme level, a red (stop operation) indicator illuminates and requires the machine to be stopped at once
and the problem corrected. (Refer to the Operator's Manual (OM) for information on these indicators.)
Diagnostic trouble codes will display on the armrest at the critical yellow stage and at the extreme (red)
stage. DTCs will stay active until the problem is resolved. (Refer to the 211 Diagnostic Trouble codes section
to diagnose.) For 610R and 616R machines that are equipped with the auxiliary oil cooler fan, the oil cooler
fan, when activated, cools oil as it is returned to the reservoir.
The PODC supplies 5 V to an internal resistor. The current is then routed out of the PODC to the hydraulic
oil temperature sensor. The PODC senses voltage at the output pin to the sensor. As the sensor
temperature increases, the resistance decreases, and the sensed voltage is lower. As the sensor
temperature decreases, the resistance increases, and the voltage increases. Sensor temperature reading is
available on the display under engine/hydraulic in the diagnostic screens.
The PODC communicates messages to the corner post display via the vehicle controller area network (CAN)
binary unit system (bus).
Hydraulic Oil Hot
When the hydraulic oil temperature is 93ΓÇö104┬░C (200ΓÇö220┬░F), the hydraulic oil temperature sensor alerts
the PODC. The PODC CAN communicates the temperature to the vehicle CAN and necessary DTCs are
displayed. The PDU will show the temperature increase on the hydraulic oil temperature indicator raising
the indicator from green to the red area.

Radar ΓÇö Electrical Theory of Operation
The radar sensors work with the speed sensors and the application system to maintain desired application
rates. Radar speed is visible on the display page. Radar speed sensor system is utilized in areas where
global positioning system (GPS) signals are poor or when wheel slip is likely to occur.
Component Information:
If a radar is installed, the sensor is at the front of the machine. The radar provides a voltage pulse signal
similar to the wheel speed sensor. The frequency of the voltage pulse is directly proportional to the
machine speed. The radar receives power from the powertrain domain control unit (PODC) when the key
switch is in either the RUN or START position.
The PODC uses the radar data to calculate speed and distance. The PODC receives the radar signal directly
from the sensor. The sensor measures the time between voltage pulses and calculates the speed. To
calculate speed accurately, the radar sensor must be calibrated. The PODC communicates the radar speed
information on the vehicle controller area network (CAN) binary unit system (bus) to the corner post
display (PDU).
When the radar speed is selected as the speed source, the PODC uses the radar signal rather than the
wheel speed sensor signal or GPS to calculate the machine speed and distance. The information is visible
on the display under the diagnostics screen.
A diagnostic trouble code (DTC) appears on the display when the radar is out of calibration. The machine is
programmed to revert to wheel speed readings if the radar signal is unavailable or vehicle speed is less
than 3.2 km/h (2 mph).
Ground for the radar system is provided by the battery box ground.
Related Information:

Grounds: Battery and Chassis ΓÇö Electrical Theory of Operation (Section 240, Group 20G)

Park Brake ΓÇö Electrical Theory of Operation
The park brake electrical system controls the flow of hydraulic oil required to desengage the spring
applied park brakes.
Component Information:
There are four ways to stop the machine. Three of these ways electrically activate the park brakes. The
fourth way, stepping on the brake pedal, activates the service brakes.
Park brake system function:
The park brake system has two modes:
At engine start, the mode is manual. Pressing the park brake switch toggles the mode between manual
and automatic.
Manual Mode
If the machine is in manual mode, the multi-function lever in neutral, and speed is less than 1.5 km/h (0.9
mph), the park brake is applied. If the multi-function lever is moved within the neutral position while in
manual mode, an alarm is presented to the operator indicating the park brake is engaged.
Automatic Mode
If the machine is in automatic mode, the multi-function lever in neutral, and speed is less than 1.5 km/h
(0.9 mph), the park brake is applied. When the multi-function lever is moved into forward or reverse,
movement of the multi-function lever sensor is detected, the park brake is released.

See & Spray Addressing ΓÇö Electrical Theory of Operation
Component Information
NOTE:
Wake-up power requires the engine running.
After the VPU receives wake-up power, the VPU begins the addressing process, which can take up to two minutes to complete. The addressing process utilizes
increasing electrical frequencies at each VPU. This allows the VPUs to identify their relative position on the boom. This relative position is used to create unique
identifiers for each VPU. These unique identifiers are then utilized whenever the VPUs report through the various controller area network (CAN) binary unit system
(bus) circuits. This enables communication on both the BoomTrac CAN bus and the respective ExactApply nozzle subnet CAN bus.
Addressing requires proper function of several circuits to complete:
Vision processing unit (VPU) assemblies

ΓÇó
Each VPU addresses with a number starting from left and going to the right.
ΓÇó
The VPU addressing circuits are connected in series. These circuits address from the two inside VPUs 
then flow out to either side.
ΓÇó
Specifically, addressing to the left of the operator's seat starts with VPU 5 and addressing circuits flow 
out to VPU 1 on the left.

4357
The address/sync circuit allows the VPU to know its physically installed location on a machine. From the address circuit frequency input, the VPU is able to report the
proper unique identifier on each CAN bus.
The VPU must claim addresses on both CAN busses. The VPU uses the same source address for all CAN busses.
Each VPU's unique location is required for See & Spray to function properly. See & Spray software uses its unique boom location to identify each camera's input, their
corresponding nozzles, and which calibrations to use. If identification of each VPU's unique boom location fails, the VPU is unable to interpret camera inputs.
Addressing works by adjusting the address/sync circuit frequency (in Hz) for each subsequent VPU. This frequency change provides a unique software identifier (VS1,
VS2, VS3, or VP1, VP2, VP3, etc.) that corresponds with each VPU number.
When any VPU is unable to address using an input frequency at power-up:
The addressing circuit is a series (daisy-chain) circuit. If the circuit is open, the daisy-chaining addressing process is unable to complete at the point of failure to
downstream VPUs. All downstream VPUs report an addressing failure. To promote uptime, the VPU has a feature in which it stores the last known successful installed
location. If the VPU is unable to address from an input frequency, it determines if it has a last stored location. If this is true, the VPU establishes its location as the
stored last known location.

[TOC-ANCHOR:sec-09001faa860ee76d]
See & Spray CAN Bus ΓÇö Electrical Theory of Operation
Component Information
Controller Area Network binary unit system (CAN bus) systems transfer messages between every control
unit on the machine. These messages include commands, requests, broadcast information, responses,
acknowledgements, and various group functions. The CAN bus is a linear network, and the control units
are connected along its length in series.
The operator has no direct control of the CAN bus systems. CAN bus operates automatically whenever the
key switch is in the ACC, RUN, or START positions.
Can Circuits
Digital messages transfer information from control unit to control unit along two circuits. One control unit
sends a message, and that message is either addressed to another control unit or to all control units. The
receiving control unit uses the information in the message to monitor or control the machine.
Each CAN bus network includes a 2.5-3.5 V CAN Hi circuit (yellow wire) and a 1.5-2.5 V CAN Lo circuit (green
wire). When no messages are being transmitted on the CAN bus, CAN bus high and CAN bus low circuits
are both approximately 2.5 V. When messages are being sent between the control units, the CAN bus high
voltage increases, and the CAN bus low voltage decreases.

[TOC-ANCHOR:sec-09001faa860ee76d]
See & Spray CAN Bus ΓÇö Electrical Theory of Operation
Component Information
Controller Area Network binary unit system (CAN bus) systems transfer messages between every control
unit on the machine. These messages include commands, requests, broadcast information, responses,
acknowledgements, and various group functions. The CAN bus is a linear network, and the control units
are connected along its length in series.
The operator has no direct control of the CAN bus systems. CAN bus operates automatically whenever the
key switch is in the ACC, RUN, or START positions.
Can Circuits
Digital messages transfer information from control unit to control unit along two circuits. One control unit
sends a message, and that message is either addressed to another control unit or to all control units. The
receiving control unit uses the information in the message to monitor or control the machine.
Each CAN bus network includes a 2.5-3.5 V CAN Hi circuit (yellow wire) and a 1.5-2.5 V CAN Lo circuit (green
wire). When no messages are being transmitted on the CAN bus, CAN bus high and CAN bus low circuits
are both approximately 2.5 V. When messages are being sent between the control units, the CAN bus high
voltage increases, and the CAN bus low voltage decreases.
CAN Terminators

PAGE 4360 | phrase: Boom CAN Bus
======================================================================
4360
Each CAN bus network has two terminators, located at each end of the CAN bus. Terminators provide the
proper resistance required between CAN Lo and high signal circuits. Terminators provide message
termination at either end of the circuit. This way, messages cannot bounce back through the circuit and
cause false signals.
Each passive CAN bus terminator is a 2-pin 120 ╬⌐ resistor.
These resistors provide passive termination ΓÇö neither power nor ground is supplied at the terminator.
These resistors regulate CAN Hi and CAN Lo circuits, verifying that each circuit stays within the appropriate
ranges.
Each active CAN bus terminator is a 6-pin or 9-pin connector. Active CAN bus terminators use machine
power to provide 12 V power and ground to two extra circuits: CAN power and CAN ground. These circuits
provide active voltage regulation and protection against changes in the magnetic field. The CAN power
and CAN ground circuits protect CAN Hi and CAN Lo circuits from reading these magnetic field changes as
false signals.
CAN Networks
Every machine has several CAN bus networks:
NOTE:
The ExactApply system can operate without the See & Spray system. However, the See & Spray
system cannot operate without the ExactApply system.
Spray CAN Bus (IB3+) ExactApply CAN Bus
Machines equipped with ExactApply (the solution spray nozzle system) are equipped with an ExactApply
CAN bus. The CAN bus connects the following control units to one another:
The MNC functions as a gateway, connecting vehicle CAN bus 1 (VB1), implement CAN bus 2 (IB1), and the
various ExactApply CAN buses (IB3, IB4, IB5, IB6). For more information about the spray CAN bus, refer to
the appropriate ExactApply technical manual.
The ExactApply CAN bus system works with the machine CAN bus system. The machine CAN bus
communicates directly to the ExactApply CAN bus in order to activate the NZCs and the MNC appropriately.
The NZCs are powered by 12 volt circuits. When the NZCs are powered, the MNC communicates to the
NZCs via the ExactApply CAN bus system for system functionality and proper solenoid timing and control.
Because of the number of NZCs on the booms, not all NZCs are on the same CAN bus circuit. The
ExactApply CAN bus is divided up into four subnets. The subnets are:
Vehicle CAN bus 1 (VB1)
1.
Implement CAN bus 2 (IB1)
2.
Boom CAN bus (IB2) (applicable only when BoomTrac Pro is equipped on the machine)
3.
Spray CAN bus (IB3+) (applicable only when ExactApply is equipped on the machine)
4.
Master Nozzle Control Unit (MNC) (when ExactApply is equipped)
ΓÇó
Individual Nozzle Control Units (NZCs) (when ExactApply is equipped)
ΓÇó
Subnet 1 (CAN bus circuit 3914 and 3915 on the far left boom)
ΓÇó
Subnet 2 (CAN bus circuit 3924 and 3925 on the mid left boom to the left center frame)
ΓÇó
Subnet 3 (CAN bus circuit 3934 and 3935 on the right center frame to the mid right boom)
ΓÇó

4362
[TOC-ANCHOR:sec-09001faa85b748b6]
See & Spray Ethernet and FAKRA ΓÇö Electrical Theory of 
Operation
Component Information
See & Spray Cameras and FAKRA Cables
Each See & Spray camera sends video information to a vision processing unit (VPU), using a non-repairable
Fachkreis Automobil (FAKRA) cable with integrated non-repairable connectors. FAKRA cables allow up to 6
GHz of information to be transmitted. FAKRA connectors mechanically lock to ensure a secure connection.
More See & Spray camera information, including how and when to calibrate these cameras, is provided in
the appropriate OperatorΓÇÖs Manual (OM).
VPUs
VPUs 1, 2, 5, and 6 connect to eight FAKRA cables and eight See & Spray cameras respectively. VPU 3
connects to four FAKRA cables and four See & Spray cameras. Each VPU processes the necessary
information and sends that information along to the appropriate See & Spray Ethernet switch, using an
Ethernet cable. The VPU periodically verifies that all of these FAKRA and Ethernet connections are
functioning correctly.
Each VPU also communicates necessary camera information through the BoomTrac CAN bus to the
gateway control unit (GWC) and through the ExactApply CAN bus to the master nozzle control unit (MNC).
This camera data provides the information necessary to automatically adjust the ExactApply nozzles (NZCs).
See & Spray Ethernet Switches and Ethernet Cables
See & Spray Ethernet switch 1 and 2, connects to four VPUs through four Ethernet cables. See & Spray
Ethernet switch 1 and 2 process the necessary information and act as a hub for See and Spray camera data.
Twisted pair circuits provide extra signal protection from magnetic influences. Ethernet cables provide
high-speed communication, which allows real-time adjustments. When needed, these Ethernet cables
provide the means to reprogram the VPUs. These Ethernet cables and integrated connectors are non-
repairable.
Ethernet Configuration 2
See & Spray Ethernet switch 1 & 2 transmits all of the See & Spray camera data information along to
configuration 2 Ethernet switch assembly, using two twisted pair Ethernet cables.
Configuration 2 Ethernet switch assembly also receives camera data from the right-hand camera and the
left-hand cameras when equipped on the machine. Each connection is made with a twisted pair of circuits.
This information plus the See & Spray camera information is sent to configuration 1 Ethernet switch
assembly, using two twisted pair Ethernet cables.

See & Spray Power and Ground ΓÇö Electrical Theory of 
Operation
Component Information
The See & Spray system power source is a constant 12 V supply that comes from the ExactApply (EA) load
center. Power to the EA load center is directly from connections at the machine batteries and battery
disconnect switch. Ground for the vision processing units is proved from the main cab ground on the
machine. Ground for the See & Spray system is provided by the cab ground, the center frame right-hand
ground buss bar and by the center frame left-hand ground buss bar.
A 250 A fuse within the mega load center battery box protects the power circuit supplied to the rear mid-
chassis load center. Power supplied to the EA load is protected by the MNC/S&S 150 A fuse within the load
center rear mid-chassis cab. The EA load center then supplies power to the See & Spray load center on the
EA power load center jumper harness.

See & Spray Load Center
The See & Spray load center (F80) is located on the top left-hand side of the fixed center frame, as facing
the rear of the machine. The load center receives supplied power on circuit (3002), protected by a 150 A
fuse (F302) in the mid-chassis power distribution load center.
The load center connectors are located behind the storage box location.
The load center supplies power to the gateway control unit (GWC) and Ethernet switches through the 5 A
Ethernet and gateway fuse. The load center supplies power to the vision processing units (VPUs) through
10 A fuses.

Ethernet and gateway fuse. The load center supplies power to the vision processing units (VPUs) through
10 A fuses.

PAGE 4366 | phrase: Gateway Control Unit

4366
[TOC-ANCHOR:sec-09001faa860fda2c]
See & Spray Wakeup ΓÇö Electrical Theory of Operation
The Gateway Control Unit provides the system wakeup power to vision processing units (VPUs). VPU
wakeup occurs in two steps, first with the lead VPU and then once active, the remaining VPUs.
The gateway costrol unit (GWC) (A725) receives wakeup power from the machine control unit wakeup
power system. Once active and either the engine is running or VPUΓÇÖs enabled using the diagnostic address,
the GWC energizes the ELX group 1 circuit, circuit 0126. ELX group 1 provides wakeup power to the lead
vision processing unit (VPU 6) (A716) and Ethernet switches 1ΓÇô3 (A726ΓÇôA728). CAN messages between VPU
5 and the GWC verify for the GWC that VPU 5 is active, allowing the GWC to energize the ELX group 2
circuit, (circuit 0136), which provides wakeup power to the remaining VPUs (A711ΓÇôA715 and A717ΓÇô720).
System shutdown follows the same process that the other machine control units follow. Messages
between the GWC and VPUs allow the controllers to shutdown before power is removed from the ELX
circuits.
Wakeup power to the VPUs and ethernet switches is provided by the GWC.
The wakeup ELX circuits are independently grounded from the machine ground via the combined ELX
ground circuits, (circits 0120/0130), to the center frame right-hand ground buss bar (GND305).

Off-Boarding VPU Logs Utilizing Service Center
When performance issues arise with See & Spray (S&S) vision processing unit (VPU) that are not identified and resolved, contact Diagnostic Technical Assistance
Center (DTAC). In order to off-board VPU logs utilizing Service Center the technician will need to contact DTAC to request diagnostic interface service cables.
Diagnostic interface service cables are not available through service parts. Due to file size of logs, the diagnostic interface service cables will aid in upload speeds.
-: Log Types and File Size
Log Type
File Size
Time Frame for Offload (Wi-Fi)*
Time Frame for Offload Cable*
Full Logs
20 GB per full log, up to 5 saved on a machine
40 min per full log

cycle OFF.

1.
Try to reprogram at least five times.
2.

3.
Try to reprogram using another method. Refer to 
 (Section 245, Group
Control Unit Reprogramming
10C).
4.
Try to reprogram using another electronic data link (EDL). If another EDL is unavailable:
5.
Log out of Service ADVISOR.
ΓÇó
Disconnect the EDL from the machine and the computer.
ΓÇó
Restart the computer.
ΓÇó
Turn off the machine for at least 30 seconds.
ΓÇó
Reconnect the EDL to both the computer and the machine.
ΓÇó
Try again.
ΓÇó
If a software data file was downloaded to the computer, delete that file and download it again.
6.
Try to reprogram using another computer.
7.
Check for contact problems or corrosion on the control unit connectors. If a contact problem exists,
pull out each pin and reinsert it into the connector. If corrosion exists, clean the connectors. Try again.
8.
NOTE:
Do not remove the following control units from the CAN bus: The control unit that is to be
reprogrammed or the operator station control unit (OSDC) with CAB software.
In certain cases, reducing the CAN bus data traffic can facilitate successful programming. Certain
control units (for example the engine control unit) transmit a large amount of data on the CAN bus.

ECU ΓÇö Electrical Theory of Operation
The engine control unit (ECU) electronically controls the functions required to monitor and operate the
diesel engine. The ECU monitors engine rpm, air temperature, coolant temperature, fuel input, and other
vital functions. Output is sent to the corner post display. If parameters are out of programmed limits, the
engine will derate or shut down if necessary.
Component Information:
Power is provided through the ECU aftertreatment fuse, ECU application fuse, and ECU engine control fuse
within the mid-chassis load center.
The ECU activates when wakeup power is supplied or when the key switch is moved out of the OFF position.
The ECU sends communications to other control units on the vehicle controller area network (CAN) binary
unit system (bus).
The ECU ground is provided by the ECU static ground and battery box ground 2 connection within the
battery box.
Related Information:
ECU ΓÇö Electrical Schematic (245-30)

GWC ΓÇö Electrical Theory of Operation
The gateway control unit (GWC) enables the See & Spray application within the display. The GWC is the
bridge between the implement controller area network (CAN) binary unit system (bus) and the See & Spray
components. If the GWC is offline, or not on the machine's implement CAN bus, the See & Spray page and
run page modules are grayed out with See & Spray disabled.
Component Information:
Unswitched power is a constant 12 V power supply that comes directly from the batteries and battery
disconnect switch. A system fuse within the battery box protects the supplied power circuit to the rear mid-
chassis cab load center. The MNC/See & Spray control unit fuse within the rear mid-chassis load center
protects the supplied power circuit to the ExactApply load center. Power is then supplied to the See &
Spray load center.
Unswitched power is provided through the gateway and Ethernet switch power fuse within the See & Spray
load center.
Switched power for the system to wake up the control units, as well as begin the proper shutdown
procedure of the control units, comes from the power train domain control unit (PODC). The PODC receives
the wakeup signal from the operator station domain control unit (OSDC). The PODC then sends 12 V to the
GWC. The GWC then relays wakeup and shutdown signals to the Ethernet switch and the vision processing
unit(s) (VPUs) through the GWC.
The GWC acts as a gateway to connect the implement CAN bus and See & Spray/BoomTrac CAN bus. The
VPUs' vision spray modules (VSMs) communicate status messages to the GWC. The GWC monitors
messages on both busses and relays the necessary information to necessary control units on the
implement bus.
The GWC allows the operator interface with VPUs VSMs and cameras on the boom through the See & Spray
screen on the display. The user can select a specific VPU VSM and camera lens. It also provides visual
feedback to what the camera is sensing by sending the information from the VPU and broadcasting the
video through ethernet from VPU to the ethernet switches and then back to the Generation 4 Display.

MTG ΓÇö Electrical Theory of Operation
The modular telematics gateway (MTG) is one of the main components that enable JDLink
communications. The MTG allows for data to transfer to and from the JDLink host server over a cellular
network or wireless network. An active JDLink subscription is required.
Component information:
Power is provided through the MTG fuse.
The MTG communicates on both the implement and vehicle controller area networks (CAN) binary unit
system (bus) systems.
The MTG activates when wakeup power is supplied or when the key switch is moved out of the OFF
position.
NOTE:
If the MTG is not properly functioning, this could affect the ethernet network for See & Spray.
The MTG ground is provided by battery box ground 2 connection within the battery box.
Related Information:

NZC ΓÇö Electrical Theory of Operation
The Master Nozzle Control Unit (MNC) operates on the implement controller area network (CAN) binary
unit system (bus). The MNC controls each nozzle body on the booms. Each nozzle body is an inidividual
nozzle control unit (NZC). All NZCs are on one of the four subnetworks (subnets) of CAN bus. There are
varying numbers of NZCs on each subnet.
Component Information:
The four subnets are:
NZCs have synchronized in-out and CAN bus in-out lines. After every power cycle, the MNC uses the
following four sync lines to establish CAN bus addresses for each of the NZCs on one of the ExactApply
subnets.
When the address sequencing is complete, the sync and CAN bus lines are used to communicate with the
MNC.
Switched battery power is provided from the ExactApply nozzles center frame fuse within the ExactApply
load center.
Wakeup is provided when the key switch is turned from the OFF position.
Ground is provided by the center frame right-hand ground.
Related Information:

PDU ΓÇö Electrical Theory of Operation
The corner post display unit (PDU) acts in conjunction with other electrical components to provide the
operator information about ground speed, engine temperature, and other machine functions.
Component Information:
The PDU power fuse provides electrical power to the PDU. However, the PDU is inactive until power is also
supplied with wakeup power. When wakeup power is removed, the PDU initiates a shutdown procedure.
The PDU uses the vehicle controller area network (CAN) binary unit system (bus) to communicate with
other control units on the machine. Presence of the PDU on the CAN bus is required for all machine
adjustments.
The PDU ground is provided by electronics battery box ground 2 connection within the battery box.
Related Information:
PDU ΓÇö Electrical Schematic (Section 245, Group 30)
Vehicle CAN Bus ΓÇö Electrical Theory of Operation (Section 240, Group 20D)
Load Center: Cab ΓÇö Electrical Theory of Operation (Section 240, Group 20G)
Grounds: Battery and Chassis ΓÇö Electrical Theory of Operation (Section 240, Group 20G)
Wakeup Power ΓÇö Electrical Theory of Operation (Section 245, Group 20)
XEC ΓÇö Cab Load Center (Section 249, Group 40F)
Grounds Overview (Section 249, Group 40X)

PAGE 5695 | phrase: Gateway Control Unit

5695
[TOC-ANCHOR:sec-09001faa861a9dd1]
VPU ΓÇö Electrical Theory of Operation
The vision processing unit (VPU) is the image processing module (IPM) that identifies live plants (green color) within an image. When an image is captured by a green
detection camera on the boom, the VPU analyzes the image for green color spectrum within the image. The VPU interprets the objects size and determines whether
to send spray message to the corresponding nozzle body to spray the object. When See & Spray Ultimate is active, only valve B of the individual nozzle responds to
commands from the VPU to spray.
Component Information:
The VPU communicates on both BoomTrac controller area network (CAN) binary unit system (bus) and the respective ExactApply nozzle subnet CAN bus. The
BoomTrac CAN bus is required to know the boom height for the proper camera region of interest to be used for image capture. The BoomTrac CAN bus also allows
for communication to the gateway control unit (GWC) for user interface to the VPU.
For correct weed analization, each aspect of the See & Spray system must communicate with each other appropriately. The cameras on the boom communicate
through coaxial cable to the VPU for weed detection. The GWC and BoomTrac communicate to the VPU through BoomTrac CAN. The individual nozzles communicate
through ExactApply CAN. Modular telematics/display communicates through the Ethernet system to the gateway control. The GWC communicates the information
back to the Generaion 4 Display on the implement CAN bus. The GWC reports issues by displaying GWC diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs).
Unswitched power is a constant 12 V power supply that comes directly from the batteries and battery disconnect switch. Power is supplied to the See & Spray load
center via the ExactApply load center. Power is supplied from the mid-chassis power distribution center to the EA load center and on to the See & Spray load center
(on the fixed center frame) with 12 V power circuit, protected by a 150A fuse master nozzle control/See & Spray fuse within the mid-chassis power distribution load
center.

Wakeup Power ΓÇö Electrical Theory of Operation
The machine uses a power management feature called wakeup power. When the control units are inactive,
the control units automatically enter a low-power state. Once the operator activates a system that
activates wakeup power, the control units are restored to an operational state.

ARMC
The CommandARM control unit (ARMC) sends wakeup power to the following:
OSDC
The operator station domain control unit (OSDC) sends wakeup power to the following:
PODC
The powertrain domain control unit (PODC) sends wakeup power to the following:
Wakeup Power Inactive
When wakeup power is removed, the control units switch to a low-power state. The low-power state is
when the following is completed:
When the key switch is in the OFF position, the OSDC maintains voltage long enough to allow the other
control units to save valuable information. Full system shutdown may take several minutes to complete.
If the horn is pressed, the OSDC will initiate wakeup even though key switch is in the OFF position.
The radio will stay active for an allotted time after the key switch is turned to the OFF position.
The battery disconnect switch indicator light continues flashing until complete system shutdown has
occurred. The disconnect switch indicator light stops flashing to inform the tech that it is now safe to
disconnect the batteries and control units.
Related Information

10┬á Procedure
Action:
IMPORTANT:
After performing this procedure, but before proceeding to the next procedure, verify that the
pins tested in this step are still fully seated and functional. Damage to pins can cause
component failure.
NOTE:
Set-up this procedure so that measurements are taken within 5 seconds of turning the machine
key switch ON. This procedure will require two technicians or test leads long enough to reach
the cab.
Do not use the black lead on the multimeter. Using the black lead and connecting to ground
can cause a false positive reading.
On the left addressing subnet, the first faulted vision processing unit (VPU) would be the
highest numbered VPU reporting as faulted. On the right addressing subnet the first faulted
VPU will be the lowest numbered VPU reporting as faulted.
Identify the first faulted VPU closest to the center of the machine by navigating to the See & Spray
application.
Key switch in the OFF position.
Identify the corresponding VPU assembly 1 connector (XA7XX-1).
With the connector still connected, connect the red lead of the multimeter to the appropriate address sync
in (pin D3) on the faulty VPU assembly 1 connector.
Key switch on the RUN position, engine running.
Measure and record the frequency.
Allow 2ΓÇö3 minutes for the VPUs to finish addressing.
Refer to the Frequency Table located in the 
 (240-
See & Spray Addressing ΓÇö Electrical Theory of Operation
20L).
Is the frequency within specification?
Result:
YES:
GO TO12
NO:
GO TO11
┬á
11┬á Procedure
Action:


======================================================================

5917
IMPORTANT:
After performing this procedure, but before proceeding to the next procedure, verify that the
pins tested in this step are still fully seated and functional. Damage to pins can cause
component failure.
Key switch in the OFF position.
Move to the next vision processing unit (VPU) closer to the center of the machine.
Identify the appropriate vision processing unit (VPU) assembly 1 connector (XA7XX-1).
With the connector still connected, connect the red lead of the multimeter to the appropriate address sync
out (pin C3) on the VPU assembly 1 connector.
Key switch on the RUN position, engine running.

 (240-

20L).

outputting the address sync signal.
To continue diagnosing an issue with the addressing circuits or the VPU, refer to the See & Spray
 (240-50L).
Addressing ΓÇö Electrical Diagnostic

N166933-UN: Flash Reprogrammer/Power Supply
NOTE:
The flash reprogrammer/power supply with battery support is specifically used when testing
the vision processing unit (VPU). This device gives extra battery support when diagnostic
testing is be performed with key switch in the OFF position or when reprogramming control
unit.

reprogramming and diagnostic work
